title: Casualty Report
subtitle: An eagle pierces through the thick black clouds of gunsmoke.

items.text: Casualty Report
They all know this aged face. He is the one who brought the gunfire and the one who now guards them.
The militia allows Igor to pass, even guiding him to where the Gryphons are now quartered.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: I'm glad to see you still remember Zeno's teachings, Ptolemy.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: When facing a bombardment, we move all vulnerable units under—
Silence. A row of bodies under white sheets.
On each pair of eyes rest two sugar cubes pressing their lids shut. Ptolemy sits behind them, shrouded in a dark shadow.

items.speaker: Ptolemy
items.text: Father ...

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: How did they die?
His son stares at the ground, unwilling to show his face. Only his trembling hands betray his emotion.

items.speaker: Gryphon Soldier
items.text: Here's a written report. For your review, Admiral.
Igor does not take the bloodied papers.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: I will hear it from him.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: Raise your head, Ptolemy. Tell me your course of action as the commander of the city operation.
He speaks calmly, but it sends a chill through the room.

items.speaker: Ptolemy
items.text: Y-Yes.

items.speaker: Ptolemy
items.text: Around sixteen hundred hours yesterday, we coordinated with the militia and Cavalry Corps to eliminate several Manus infantry squads that had infiltrated the city.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: You already reported that during our last communication.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: And after the signal was jammed?

items.speaker: Ptolemy
items.text: I dispatched an ad hoc squad to investigate the source of the signal interference. Five arcanist infantry troopers and two technicians. Yaroslav Levchuk was the squad leader.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: What else did you order them to do?
His father has torn away the veil. While shame burns Ptolemy's face, fear freezes his words.

items.speaker: Ptolemy
items.text: I-I ordered them to sneak into the forest.

items.speaker: Ptolemy
items.text: To find traces of Krutov at any cost.

items.speaker: Ptolemy
items.text: And then, six corpses were delivered to the entrance of our base.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: You allowed yourself to be blinded with hatred, Ptolemy. How can I entrust you with the Gryphon Legion if you can't maintain a steady hand?

items.speaker: Ptolemy
items.text: I know, Father. I made a grave mistake. I will accept whatever punishment you see fit.
He pauses, the ache in his left eye socket betraying a resentment rarely shown in front of his father.

items.speaker: Ptolemy
items.text: But Krutov ... I saw him! He was right there, hiding in the woods!

items.speaker: Ptolemy
items.text: I was so close I could see that arrogant sneer of his, hear the incessant classical music playing from his tent!

items.speaker: Ptolemy
items.text: You know what he did to me, to us!

items.speaker: Ptolemy
items.text: Every time I hear that wretched name, my eye aches with unbearable pain.
A strange ceiling. A sharp, throbbing pain. Half the world has gone dark.

items.speaker: Ptolemy
items.text: Agh, ah, medic! Medic! I need morphine!

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: They just gave you some, Ptolemy.

items.speaker: Ptolemy
items.text: Moldir, what happened? Did our convoy hit a booby trap?

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: No, not a booby trap.

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: Enemies disguised as civilians were lurking by the farms you passed through. No one expected them to be hiding explosive Blazefuse cylinders beneath their clothes.

items.speaker: Ptolemy
items.text: Right, right. I remember. My eye ... When will it be healed?

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: The retina in your left eye took a severe burn in the explosion. I'll see to it that you recover as much as possible. For now, just rest.
He understands what this means. He'll have to learn to fire from his other shoulder.

items.speaker: Ptolemy
items.text: Is Captain Krutov alright? We were in the same car.

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: He only suffered a mild concussion, thanks to you. I doubt he would have survived if you hadn't pushed him off in time.

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: You should sleep, brother. I'll ask the medic to increase your dosage.
Ptolemy grips her arm tightly.

items.speaker: Ptolemy
items.text: Did we win?

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: Of course. Father's strategy was effective as always. We destroyed the enemy command post. We took sector four decisively.

items.speaker: Ptolemy
items.text: Good.

items.speaker: Ptolemy
items.text: You need to rest too, Molly. And don't send for the medic. I don't need morphine anymore.

items.speaker: Ptolemy
items.text: As we left Antarctica, I saw the documents those traitors tried to steal from your bag.

items.speaker: Ptolemy
items.text: I learned what Krutov did—staging an assassination on himself, making it look like an enemy ambush—just to pressure the Foundation into approving the use of high-risk arcane weapons!

items.speaker: Ptolemy
items.text: Killing me was part of his plan all along! I only survived because the assassin hesitated when I tried to save him!

items.speaker: Ptolemy
items.text: Father, why did you keep this from me?

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: Anger would only cloud your judgment, as proved with your actions.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: You will have your revenge, an eye for an eye. I promise you.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: But now, you must bear responsibility for your mistakes and honor the sacrifice of your brothers.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: They gave up past glory, identity, and every proof of their existence for us, entrusting the future into my hands.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: Do you not remember what I told you after leaving São Paulo?

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: No more meaningless sacrifices. We don't leave anyone behind. You speak with my voice; you should remember this more than anyone.

items.speaker: Ptolemy
items.text: I will, Father.
Ptolemy touches the bandage over his burning eye socket and nods, willing himself to remain steady.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: What's that noise? I thought communications were severed after Krutov's assault.

items.speaker: Ptolemy
items.text: We managed to reestablish a signal. It's been up nearly half an hour, but the only thing it's picked up is some bizarre enemy frequency.

items.speaker: Ptolemy
items.text: The operators think it's some form of interference intended to jam our signals, so they've muted it.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: You mean this noise is a signal from Krutov's army, from Manus Vindictae?

items.speaker: Ptolemy
items.text: Well, in theory, yes.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: Bring it up and unmute it! Now!

items.speaker: Ptolemy
items.text: Yes, sir!
He cuts all the jamming signals at once and turns the volume to its maximum.
The "enemy radio station" crackles to life. Faint gunfire sounds in the background.
Falcon Six calling the nest. Falcon Six calling the nest. This is the 45th call. Please respond!
Huh? What? Is it connected? Command, do you copy?

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: We read you loud and clear.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: This is your commander. Report your status.
